text:
tara: Quick favor — can someone run perf checks on the kernel-op-fusion branch? We merged PR #847. Looking for throughput and mem usage for the FlashAttention path. Target rigs: a100-40gb, sequences 128 & 4096, batches 1/8/32. Please run with commit 9f3b2c1 and image redwood/runtime:canary-847.

amir: I can take it. Do you want raw nvprof traces or the microbench harness numbers?

tara: Harness numbers for a short summary + nvprof if you see anything weird. Use the bench in tools/perf/flash_bench.py. Example command: 

``
python tools/perf/flash_bench.py --model gpt-j --commit 9f3b2c1 --device a100 --seq 4096 --batch 1 --iters 100
```

also run with `--enable-fusion true` and `--enable-fusion false` and post both.

amir: Running now on a100-40gb. Will post p50/p90/p99 and peak mem. ETA ~30m.

perf-bot: queued benchmark job 9472 for commit 9f3b2c1 on a100-40gb.

amir: quick results (canary vs baseline master):
- seq=128, batch=32: canary throughput 980 tok/s vs baseline 965 tok/s (+1.6%), p99 slightly better
- seq=128, batch=1: canary 210 tok/s vs baseline 225 (-6.7%) regression
- seq=4096, batch=1: canary 14.2 tok/s vs baseline 11.8 (+20.3%) win
- mem peak: canary +1.8GB on seq=4096 (likely kernel temporary workspace)

Logs:
``
[run] commit=9f3b2c1 device=a100 seq=4096 batch=1 iters=100
tokens/sec: 14.2 p50=70ms p90=120ms p99=190ms peak_mem=35.4GB
cuda kernel fused_attn_v2 launched 1.8ms
```

joel: interesting mixed results. The short-seq regression suggests fusion overhead for small contexts. Can you re-run seq=128 with `--prefetch-kv=false` and `--enable-fusion=true`? Also try `TORCH_USE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` (env).

amir: re-ran seq=128,batch=1 with prefetch_kv disabled + cuda_graph env:
- canary: 233 tok/s (now +3.5% vs baseline)
- peak mem unchanged
So prefetch + fusion interaction looks bad for small seq.

sophie: for rollout gating — can we add a perf smoke in CI? e.g. run seq=4096,batch=1 on a minimal harness and require no >10% regression on p50. That would catch big regressions like the long-run win/loss.

tara: yes. @joel can you add a quick smoke (image canary-847) to the perf-gate job? If short-seq regressions persist, we can disable fusion by default and expose a flag.

joel: will do. I'll add a new job `kernel-fusion-smoke` with thresholds and a mem delta assert (peak_mem delta < 2GB for long runs). Also add an env toggle to CI to test prefetch_kv combinations.

perf-bot: benchmark 9472 completed. Summary: [seq128,b32:+1.6%] [seq128,b1:-6.7% -> repro with prefetch_kv=true] [seq4096,b1:+20%]. Details: https://perf.redwood/9472

amir: dug in — found the workspace allocation path in fused kernel that scales with prefetch_kv=true; opened PR #852 with a fix and a repro script. Ran quick bench against #852 and seq128 returns to baseline.

tara: awesome. Action items: amir -> verify PR #852 fixes seq128 regressions and push canary; joel -> add perf smoke in CI (kernel-fusion-smoke); sophie -> add gating policy doc for perf regressions; I'll coordinate canary rollout and tell infra to monitor mem spikes.

amir: PR #852 is up, I attached nvprof traces and before/after numbers in the PR description. LMK if you want the full traces uploaded to the perf bucket.

tara: please upload traces and link in PR. If CI smoke passes, we'll flip fusion=true in canary rollout for a subset of traffic.

joel: added the smoke job branch in perf-ci, threshold files at infra/perf/thresholds/kernel_fusion.json. Putting a safety flag so fusion is disabled by default in perf gate.

perf-bot: perf smoke job kernel-fusion-smoke queued on canary image canary-847 (job 9480).

amir: re-run of full matrix after #852: seq128,b1 -> 226 tok/s (baseline 225), seq4096,b1 -> 15.1 tok/s (improved). Mem delta now +0.3GB.

tara: excellent. Final: if perf gate passes tomorrow we'll schedule canary rollout. Thanks all :thumbsup:
__notes: Generated Slack thread for kernel/attention optimization experiments, focused on FlashAttention, fusion flags, profiling, and CI gating. Conforms to agents.md: single continuous string, messages prefixed with sender names, metadata fields present.
